requirements.title: Complete Style Set Across Word Templates

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Attached are the files and the brief. I look forward to hearing your assessment.

We are seeking an experienced Microsoft Word template specialist to inspect, correct, and enhance a collection of Word templates intended for the latest Microsoft Word versions on Windows PC.

This is not purely visual work. The templates must also be technically reliable under real user behavior, particularly when users copy and paste content from older legacy templates into the new ones.

**The assistance we would appreciate.**

1\. Carefully review this brief
2\. Examine the newest template documents together with the supporting files
3\. Respond with:
• a fixed price for the project
• a suggested timeline
• any early observations or potential risks

⸻

Work Scope

1\. Evaluate the existing templates

Conduct user and functional testing of the current templates to confirm that they are constructed properly and work dependably during ordinary day-to-day use.

Testing covers:
• styles
• list behavior
• indentation logic
• tab behavior
• line breaks
• tables
• columns
• copy-paste behavior
• overall formatting stability

⸻

2\. Apply new styles to every template

Introduce the new style system specified in this document:

new\_styles\_for\_implementation\_pbu

The system must be implemented consistently in all templates.

⸻

3\. Recommend enhancements

Assess the templates and propose both:
• need-to-have improvements
• nice-to-have improvements

Recommendations may cover missing functionality, structural changes, usability enhancements, or technical corrections that would improve template stability and ease of use.

⸻

Operating Environment

Every template will be used with the latest Microsoft Word versions on PC.

They should be optimized for:
• modern Word for Windows
• actual user editing behavior
• reliable usage by multiple users

⸻

Customer Design Feedback Requiring Implementation

A. Indentation logic and Tab functionality

For all applicable list styles, users must be able to naturally create sub-levels with the Tab key.

Requirements:
• every list style must allow intuitive indentation into sub-levels
• the hierarchy must stay organized and clean
• list levels must adhere to the vertical alignment logic illustrated in the brief
• nested levels must maintain consistent alignment across the document

(Refer to New\_styles\_for\_implementation\_pbu for the design guides)

B. Graphic bullet design

Revise the bullet formatting so:
• bullet size remains proportional to text size
• bullets have visual balance
• bullets are vertically centered against the text
• bullets scale naturally according to font size

C. Rename every style

If it is relevant to resolving copy paste isuues, rename all template styles using this prefix:

PBU -

Examples:
• PBU - Heading 1
• PBU - Body Text
• PBU - Bullet List

This requirement covers every relevant style, including:
• headings
• body text
• quotes
• list styles
• table-related styles
• other active styles used in the templates

⸻

Customer-Reported Errors to Fix

1\. Compatibility and copy-paste stability

Users currently encounter significant formatting problems when transferring content from older templates into the new templates.

The following old templates have been supplied for testing:
• Old\_v1.docx
• Old\_v2.docx

This workflow must be tested and made as stable as possible.

2\. Problems with line breaks

Correct the problem that prevents users from consistently inserting manual line breaks after pasted material.

3\. Integrity of tables and columns

Resolve the problems where:
• pasting causes the right-hand column to shift beyond the page margins
• table layouts become broken after content is pasted

The table structure must stay locked, stable, and inside the page layout.

4\. Preventing style breakage

Determine whether template styles can be made less likely to break, or prevented from breaking, when users paste text from legacy documents.

We recognize that Word has limitations, but the goal is the most robust configuration technically possible.

⸻

Testing Expectations

Carry out comprehensive testing for:
• all list levels
• bullet lists
• numbered lists
• multilevel list behavior
• tab and indent behavior
• table behavior
• column behavior
• copying and pasting from legacy templates
• manual line breaks following pasted content
• overall layout stability

Specific testing requirement

In particular, test copying and pasting from old PBU templates into V14 and confirm that:
• the layout stays stable
• style behavior is predictable
• end users can use the Tab functionality intuitively
• list hierarchy stays aligned and usable

⸻

Required Deliverables

Your proposal should contain:
1\. A fixed project price
2\. An estimated timeline
3\. notes covering suggested need-to-have and nice-to-have improvements

Upon delivery, we expect:
• revised template files
• consistent PBU style naming (maybe)
• the new styles implemented (Refer to New\_styles\_for\_implementation\_pbu for design guides)
• better list behavior
• greater paste stability wherever technically possible

source_message.text:
Salma [FREELANCER_NAME_001]

Below is the initial feedback from our customer. Tell me what you think.

Proposal \(Indstilling\):
• Placeholder fields: Unlike the behavior in the Executive Summary, clicking the "insert" fields \(Advantages, settings, attachments, headline, and date\) does not automatically clear the existing text.

• Line breaks: As a result, users must insert line breaks manually. Unfortunately, using a "normal" line break \(hard return\) creates too much line spacing. That spacing works well between bullet points, but it is excessive for continuous text. A "soft return" \(Shift\+Enter\) does work, although I doubt our colleagues know how to use it.
• Date function: Could the same date functionality used in the "Board Seminar" document be implemented here?
Guidance \(Vejledning\):
• Margins: The margins beneath the "\(short description\)" section are not fixed. If you don't add manual line breaks, the "pencil" icon is gradually cut off. Can the margins be fixed?
• Theme description: This has the same problem described in point 3 under "Proposal."
• Reflections: Beneath "\(write own reflections, if any\)," there is the same issue described in point 1 under "Proposal."
Board Seminar \(Bestyrelsesseminar\):
• Multi-line support: Users must be able to enter multiple lines beneath "Item and Title." Manual line breaks need to work here.
• Agenda: Beneath "\(insert agenda\)," the issue is the same as point 1 under "Proposal."
Board Meeting \(Bestyrelsesmøde\):
• Date function: Can this have the same date functionality as the "Board Seminar" document?
• Alignment: "Item and Title" do not line up with "Topic," "Proposal," and "Start time."
• Formatting issues: Adding an extra line directly after a "Topic" also creates an additional horizontal line/border. Adding a line anywhere else behaves as intended.
Master:
• Review: We must review this with [CLIENT_NAME_001] because the bullet sizes and spacing still look incorrect on my screen.
• Tables: I need a walkthrough/explanation showing how the tables function.
• Color palette: All of these colors should not be available as options.

value_updates.color_availability_policy: Only the approved template colors should be available; inappropriate additional colors must not be exposed as options.

This is not purely visual work. The templates must also be technically reliable under real user behavior, particularly when users copy and paste content from older legacy templates into the new ones.

**The assistance we would appreciate.**

1\. Carefully review this brief
2\. Examine the newest template documents together with the supporting files
3\. Respond with:
• a fixed price for the project
• a suggested timeline
• any early observations or potential risks

⸻

Work Scope

1\. Evaluate the existing templates

Conduct user and functional testing of the current templates to confirm that they are constructed properly and work dependably during ordinary day-to-day use.

Testing covers:
• styles
• list behavior
• indentation logic
• tab behavior
• line breaks
• tables
• columns
• copy-paste behavior
• overall formatting stability

⸻

2\. Apply new styles to every template

Introduce the new style system specified in this document:

new\_styles\_for\_implementation\_pbu

The system must be implemented consistently in all templates.

⸻

3\. Recommend enhancements

Assess the templates and propose both:
• need-to-have improvements
• nice-to-have improvements

Recommendations may cover missing functionality, structural changes, usability enhancements, or technical corrections that would improve template stability and ease of use.

⸻

Operating Environment

Every template will be used with the latest Microsoft Word versions on PC.

They should be optimized for:
• modern Word for Windows
• actual user editing behavior
• reliable usage by multiple users

⸻

A. Indentation logic and Tab functionality

For all applicable list styles, users must be able to naturally create sub-levels with the Tab key.

Requirements:
• every list style must allow intuitive indentation into sub-levels
• the hierarchy must stay organized and clean
• list levels must adhere to the vertical alignment logic illustrated in the brief
• nested levels must maintain consistent alignment across the document

(Refer to New\_styles\_for\_implementation\_pbu for the design guides)

B. Graphic bullet design

Revise the bullet formatting so:
• bullet size remains proportional to text size
• bullets have visual balance
• bullets are vertically centered against the text
• bullets scale naturally according to font size

If it is relevant to resolving copy paste isuues, rename all template styles using this prefix:

PBU -

Examples:
• PBU - Heading 1
• PBU - Body Text
• PBU - Bullet List

This requirement covers every relevant style, including:
• headings
• body text
• quotes
• list styles
• table-related styles
• other active styles used in the templates

• Old\_v1.docx
• Old\_v2.docx

Correct the problem that prevents users from consistently inserting manual line breaks after pasted material.

• pasting causes the right-hand column to shift beyond the page margins
• table layouts become broken after content is pasted

Determine whether template styles can be made less likely to break, or prevented from breaking, when users paste text from legacy documents.

• all list levels
• bullet lists
• numbered lists
• multilevel list behavior
• tab and indent behavior
• table behavior
• column behavior
• copying and pasting from legacy templates
• manual line breaks following pasted content
• overall layout stability

• the layout stays stable
• style behavior is predictable
• end users can use the Tab functionality intuitively
• list hierarchy stays aligned and usable

• better list behavior
• greater paste stability wherever technically possible
